question: For what value of \(n\) is \[ \begin{aligned} &i + 2i^2 + 3i^3 + \cdots + ni^n \\ &= 48 + 49i? \end{aligned} \] Note: here \(i = \sqrt{-1}.\)
solution:
The powers of \(i\) repeat as \(i,-1,-i,1\), so grouping four consecutive terms makes the growing coefficients cancel in pairs. For every integer \(j\ge0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(4j+1)i^{4j+1}+(4j+2)i^{4j+2}\\
&\quad +(4j+3)i^{4j+3}+(4j+4)i^{4j+4}\\
&=(4j+1)i-(4j+2)-(4j+3)i+(4j+4)\\
&=2-2i.
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(S_n=i+2i^2+\cdots+ni^n\), with \(S_0=0\). After \(q\) complete blocks, adding zero, one, two, or three more terms gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{4q}&=2q-2qi,\\
S_{4q+1}&=2q+(2q+1)i,\\
S_{4q+2}&=-(2q+2)+(2q+1)i,\\
S_{4q+3}&=-(2q+2)-(2q+2)i.
\end{aligned}
\]
These four cases cover every positive integer \(n\) exactly once. Since \(48+49i\) has both parts positive, only the case \(n=4q+1\) is possible. Comparing real parts gives \(2q=48\), so \(q=24\). The imaginary part is then \(2q+1=49\), as required.

Thus \(n=4(24)+1=\boxed{97}\), choice D.
